bull.b: The predominance of subscription revenue gives Braze a recurring foundation and supports more predictable monetization than a services-led model. As customers expand channels, data usage, and messaging volumes, the usage-scaled SaaS structure can support durable revenue growth and deeper account relationships.

Net retention above 100% shows that Braze is expanding revenue within its existing customer base, not relying solely on new-logo wins. Large-account retention of 112% is especially supportive of durable growth because enterprise expansions, renewals, and broader channel adoption can compound over multiple periods.

Positive and growing free cash flow, combined with substantial liquidity, improves Braze's ability to fund product development, sales capacity, and AI initiatives internally. This reduces dependence on external financing while giving management flexibility to invest through changing enterprise software conditions.

bear.b: Braze remains unprofitable on a GAAP basis, so strong revenue growth has not yet translated into positive operating and net earnings. Continued losses can constrain long-term capital allocation and leave the business needing sustained execution before its growth model produces durable shareholder returns.

Gross-margin pressure from higher premium messaging volumes and added Decisioning Studio cost of revenue could limit operating leverage as the product mix evolves. If these costs persist while AI and messaging adoption increase, revenue growth may translate less efficiently into cash flow and profit.

The extended migration to new pricing and packaging creates execution and comparability risk across subscription and services revenue. Reclassification of previously bundled revenue may obscure underlying growth, while customer transitions and pricing changes could temporarily affect renewals, expansion timing, and reported mix.
